cases.name: Melinda Brown
cases.narrative:
On 11/25/1998, her remains were found next to a shallow grave a couple hundred yards off a popular dirt road in the Hungry Valley area of Los Padres National Forest near Gorman.

"There was a lot of animal activity,” says Ventura County Sheriff’s Office Sgt. Craig Hennes. “It looked like some of the wildlife had unearthed her and dragged her out of the shallow grave.”

She had been shot in the back, he says.

cases.name: Jessica Tinoco
cases.about:
Tinoco grew up in Oxnard. She and her children moved to Simi Valley several years ago.

“She was my family, we were really close,” said Alesha Alonzo, who met Tinoco in elementary school.

Alonzo said Tinoco—who most recently worked as a receptionist—was a devoted single mom who always made sure the children had a roof over their heads and were provided for.

“She was the strongest woman I knew. She had the biggest heart. Everything she did was for her kids. She was the most loving mom,” Alonzo said.

“She was a very dedicated mother before anything. She loved family and being with family. She was just an awesome, loving person and she did not deserve this at all,” Alonzo said.
